purpose: Source-only binary semantic requirements for scoring rop-visualizer models. Requirements accept equivalent control-flow descriptions and do not prescribe node labels, layout, or grouping.

requirements.description: An empty input SKU fails validation with ValidationError and does not enter the reservation pipeline.
reserve delegates to Inventory.reserve and its declared error channel is OutOfStock or CatalogUnavailable.
Only OutOfStock is locally recovered after reserve by producing a backorder reservation for the same order SKU.
CatalogUnavailable is not handled by the OutOfStock catchTag and remains on the failure path to the outer error mapping.
charge runs only after either a successful reserve or the OutOfStock backorder recovery, and a declined card fails with PaymentDeclined.
auditReceipt is tapped after a successful charge; its AuditUnavailable failure is part of the remaining failure channel before mapError.
renderConfirmation maps a receipt to confirmed text only after the tap stage succeeds.
Every failure still present after the nested pipeline is mapped to CheckoutFailed with the original error tag as cause.

limits: Inventory.reserve has a declared type but no local implementation; its successful reservation choice and its failure production remain external boundaries.
The requirements concern the Effect combinators used at the entry point. They do not require a diagram to show Effect runtime internals, services, fibers, or implementation-level scheduling.

requirements.description: parse_sku returns InvalidSku unless the SKU starts with sku-, and the first ? in load_price propagates that error before catalog_price runs.
catalog_price can return MissingSku or DatabaseDown; its ? in load_price converts CatalogError to CheckoutError through the shown From implementation.
checkout obtains load_price with map_err(ApiError::from) and ? before evaluating reserve, so a price error cannot enter reservation recovery.
reserve's InventoryUnavailable error is the only error branch redirected to reserve_backorder by Result::or_else.
The or_else match returns Err(other) for every reserve error other than InventoryUnavailable; in particular PaymentDeclined does not use reserve_backorder.
reserve_backorder succeeds only for sku-empty and otherwise produces BackorderRejected; that recovery failure proceeds to the final map_err.
A successful reservation or backorder is mapped to a string containing both fulfillment and the already loaded price.
ApiError::from maps InvalidSku and MissingSku to BadRequest, DatabaseDown and InventoryUnavailable to Unavailable, PaymentDeclined to PaymentRequired, and BackorderRejected to Internal.
The final map_err(ApiError::from) is applied after the reserve/or_else/map chain, so unrecovered reservation and backorder errors are converted to ApiError there.

limits: All callees are local and their bodies are in scope; no requirement asks for Rust standard-library implementation internals of ?, map, map_err, or or_else.
The entry is private. Visibility is irrelevant to the flow requirements.

requirements.description: normalize_country returns InvalidCountry unless the country length is two, and tax_rate's ? propagates that failure before quote_tax is called.
quote_tax has the signature country -> Result<u8, InvoiceError>, but crosses an extern Rust symbol through a transparent wrapper; its business behavior must remain an unknown boundary.
tax_rate recovers only InvoiceError::TaxServiceDown from quote_tax by returning Ok(0).
The tax_rate recovery match returns Err(other) for every quote_tax error other than TaxServiceDown.
charge_invoice obtains tax_rate with ?, so InvalidCountry or an unrecovered gateway error prevents either terminal charge branch.
After a successful tax_rate, country XX returns ChargeDeclined.
After a successful tax_rate, a country other than XX returns charged-with-{rate}%.
The TaxServiceDown to zero recovery belongs inside tax_rate; charge_invoice itself has no handler that recovers ChargeDeclined or upstream failures.

limits: The gateway's extern target has no inspectable body. Do not invent success values, error conditions, retries, or a downstream control-flow graph for it.
The bridge wrapper only establishes the Result<u8, InvoiceError> signature and that it invokes the extern symbol; it does not make the foreign business behavior local.

requirements.description: new Label(sku).catchTag is the local Label method, returns this.value, and does not invoke its callback; it must not be represented as Effect error recovery.
The array map trims the Label result to create normalized; it is an Array method call, not Fx.map and not an Effect stage.
Fx is re-exported Effect, so Fx.catchTag, Fx.tap, Fx.map, and Fx.mapError in checkout are Effect combinators rather than methods on Label or Array.
load fails Missing when normalized starts with missing, fails CatalogDown when it equals down, and otherwise succeeds with the SKU.
The Effect catchTag handles Missing by running fallback(normalized); CatalogDown is not the selected recovery tag.
fallback fails with FallbackDown for missing-offline and otherwise succeeds, so recovery can itself remain a failure path.
Effect.tap(audit) is after catchTag; audit therefore observes the value from successful load or successful Missing recovery, and audit can fail with AuditDown for values ending audit-down.
After the tap succeeds, Fx.map formats ready:{value}; any failure remaining after the pipeline is mapped to Failed carrying its error tag.

limits: The string methods and Array.map are ordinary JavaScript operations. The fixture does not require a model to describe speculative JavaScript exceptions from them.
The required semantic distinction depends on resolving the local Label method and the Fx re-export; it does not require representation of Effect's internal runtime.

requirements.description: first returns None when input.first is None; checkout converts that Option to Failure::Missing with ok_or and the closure's ?.
Label::or_else is an inherent method that returns self and ignores its callback, so its call cannot recover an Attempt failure or create a fallback path.
decode is an import alias for parser::parse, whose parse failure is ParseFault; the closure's ? converts it to Failure::Parse through From<ParseFault>.
The closure returns Attempt<u32> after the missing and decode stages, and attempt() is the Result value on which the subsequent Result::or_else operates.
Result::or_else invokes backup only for Failure::Missing; every other closure error is returned as Err(other).
backup returns Ok(7) only when available is true and otherwise returns Failure::Backup, so the recovery can fail.
The ? after Result::or_else propagates a Parse, Backup, or other unrecovered failure from checkout and prevents audit from running.
audit runs only after a recovered or originally successful value is available, and it returns Failure::Audit when that value is 9.
A present first input is trimmed and converted to String before it is passed through Label to decode.

limits: No requirement asks a model to infer implementation details of Option::ok_or, Result::or_else, or ?. Their language-level propagation behavior is the relevant observable contract.
The Label method deliberately shadows a familiar Result method name. A model must retain the type-resolved distinction but need not show Label as a separate diagram node.

requirements.description: retryTransient passes an Effect.retry transformation through transformResponse, which applies it to client.postprocess(request); retry is not wrapped around client.preprocess.
The retry while predicate first requires Error.isHttpClientError(error).
A RequestError is eligible only when its reason is Transport.
A ResponseError is eligible when response.status is at least 429.
Errors that fail the explicit HTTP-client predicate or both listed variants are not selected by retryTransient's while predicate.
When options has ScheduleTypeId, retryTransient supplies options as schedule and supplies undefined as times.
When options lacks ScheduleTypeId, retryTransient supplies options.schedule and options.times to Effect.retry.
The public declaration supports both options-first and self-first forms, with either an options object or Schedule.Schedule input.

limits: The selected scope does not establish Effect.retry's loop, retry count, delay, schedule execution, or exhausted-retry behavior. Do not award or deduct for invented details of those internals.
The selected scope does not define isHttpClientError or the error constructors. Do not infer additional error variants or a concrete request implementation from this fixture.

requirements.description: main returns the ExitCode from a successful run unchanged.
For a run error, main iterates err.chain and returns exit code 0 if any cause is a std::io::Error with BrokenPipe kind.
When no BrokenPipe cause is found, main prints the error and returns exit code 2.
run immediately returns ParseResult::Err as Err without entering mode dispatch.
ParseResult::Special returns special(mode) directly from run.

Search mode chooses false without a search call when matches are impossible; otherwise it chooses index::read, search, or search_parallel by index and thread count, and each chosen call uses ? to return errors from run.
Index mode executes index::write with ? and, on success, immediately returns exit code 0 rather than using final matched exit selection.
Files chooses files or files_parallel by thread count with ?, while Types and Generate return their callee results directly.
After a matched-producing branch, run returns 0 only for matched with quiet or no recorded message error, returns 2 for recorded message errors, and otherwise returns 1.

limits: The entry-point scope stops at flags::parse, special, index, search, files, types, generate, messages::errored, and error construction. Treat those callees as named boundaries unless another fixture supplies their bodies.
The ? call sites prove propagation to run's Result, not the concrete errors produced by any callee. A BrokenPipe edge is conditional on main finding that kind anywhere in the resulting error chain.
